items.name: Anger cycle diagram
items.body:
The anger cycle â how anger builds.
1 Trigger â something happens (I'm told what to do, I'm laughed at, I'm interrupted)
2 Body signals â my body reacts (clenched fists, hot face, fast heartbeat)
3 Thoughts â what I tell myself ("this isn't fair", "they're against me")
4 Action â what I do next (shout, push, walk away, use a strategy)
The cycle repeats â the action at step 4 often shapes the next trigger. Catching it early, at step 1 or 2, is the
goal.

items.name: Nicotine cycle diagram
items.body:
How the nicotine cycle works.
1. Craving builds: the brain signals it wants nicotine
2. Use: vaping delivers a fast hit of nicotine
3. Short dopamine boost: a brief feel-good effect
4. Dip: the feeling fades, often below where it started
5. Craving builds again: the cycle repeats

items.name: What counts as cyberbullying briefing card
items.body:
Cyberbullying can take many forms.
ï· Being excluded from group chats deliberately
ï· Nasty comments or messages, repeated or one-off
ï· Sharing embarrassing content without consent
ï· Impersonation or fake accounts
ï· It can follow you home: that makes it different from in-person bullying

ï· "Everyone else finds this easier than me", most people feel this way privately

items.name: Revision session length guide
items.body:
Short, regular sessions work better than long ones.

ï· Rest is part of the plan, not a reward for finishing

items.body:
A simple technique to practise ahead of time.
ï· Breathe in slowly for a count of 4
ï· Hold for a count of 2
ï· Breathe out slowly for a count of 6
ï· Repeat 4-5 times

items.body:

items.name: What makes a relationship feel safe? briefing card
items.body:
Features of a healthy relationship.
ï· Mutual respect and equal say
ï· No pressure to keep secrets from people who care about you
ï· A 'no' is respected without punishment
ï· You feel like yourself around them, not smaller

items.name: Grooming and exploitation tactics card set
items.body:
Common tactics, explained plainly.
ï· Being singled out for special attention
ï· Gifts or money that create a sense of obligation
ï· Being isolated from friends or family
ï· Being told to keep secrets from people who care about you

items.name: Why it's hard to spot briefing note
items.body:
These tactics work because they don't feel wrong at first.
ï· Attention can feel flattering before it feels controlling
ï· Small favours can build a sense of debt gradually
ï· Isolation often happens slowly, one friendship at a time
ï· It's never the young person's fault if this happens to them
